CWE-22.name: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')
CWE-22.original_description: The product uses external input to construct a pathname that is intended to identify a file or directory that is located underneath a restricted parent directory, but the product does not properly neutralize special elements within the pathname that can cause the pathname to resolve to a location that is outside of the restricted directory.
CWE-22.description: Path traversal in Python web and CLI code when user-controlled path segments are joined and opened without canonicalization or a directory jail. Common in Flask/Django file download/upload handlers, static file helpers, and scripts that build paths with os.path.join or pathlib and then open/read/write.
CWE-22.detection_notes: Python-oriented (future detector): taint from request args/forms/CLI argv into os.path.join, pathlib.Path operations, open(), pathlib.Path.open, shutil.copy*, send_file / send_from_directory (Flask), FileResponse (Django/Starlette) without resolve()+prefix checks. Flag .. segments and absolute paths mixed into restricted roots. Prefer pathlib.Path.resolve() under an allowlisted base and reject escapes.

CWE-78.name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')
CWE-78.original_description: The product constructs all or part of an OS command using externally-influenced input from an upstream component, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes special elements that could modify the intended OS command when it is sent to a downstream component.
CWE-78.description: OS command injection in Python when externally influenced data reaches a shell or argument vector without safe argv separation. Typical sinks: subprocess with shell=True, os.system, os.popen, and string-built command lines passed to asyncio.create_subprocess_shell.
CWE-78.detection_notes: Python-oriented (future detector): taint into subprocess.run/Popen/call/check_output with shell=True; os.system; os.popen; asyncio.create_subprocess_shell; and any format/f-string/join building a shell command string. Prefer subprocess with a list argv and shell=False; avoid interpolating untrusted data into shell strings. Review shlex usage only as a partial mitigation.

CWE-79.name: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')
CWE-79.original_description: The product does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes user-controllable input before it is placed in output that is used as a web page that is served to other users.
CWE-79.description: Cross-site scripting when Python web apps emit user-controlled data into HTML/JS contexts without escaping. Common with Jinja2 autoescape disabled, |safe / Markup() on untrusted values, Django templates marked safe, or responses built with raw HTML string concatenation.
CWE-79.detection_notes: Python-oriented (future detector): taint from request data into template renders with autoescape=False; Jinja2 Markup() / |safe; Django mark_safe / SafeString; Flask/Starlette/Django responses that set text/html from formatted user input; and f-strings building HTML. Prefer engine autoescape, context-aware escaping, and Content-Type discipline. Attribute/JS contexts need stronger sinks than HTML body escaping alone.

CWE-89.name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection')
CWE-89.original_description: The product constructs all or part of an SQL command using externally-influenced input from an upstream component, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes special elements that could modify the intended SQL command when it is sent to a downstream component.
CWE-89.description: SQL injection in Python when untrusted input is concatenated or formatted into SQL instead of bound parameters. Seen with DB-API cursor.execute on f-strings/percent-format, SQLAlchemy text() with format/f-string, Django raw()/extra() with unsanitized fragments, and similar ORM escape hatches.
CWE-89.detection_notes: Python-oriented (future detector): taint into sqlite3/psycopg/MySQLdb/pymysql cursor.execute/executemany when the SQL string is built via f-string, format, %, or + with non-constant parts; SQLAlchemy text()/format_sql patterns; Django QuerySet.raw / .extra / cursor.execute. Prefer parameter binding (%s, ?, :name) and ORM APIs; never format user input into the SQL string body.
